title: Quarterly options expiration — triple witching (March 2027)
source: EST: derived from the standing third-Friday-of-the-quarter-month convention this calendar's other opex entries (opex-2026-11-20, opex-2026-12-18) already encode, with the weekday arithmetic computed mechanically by this session on 2026-09-05 — the third Friday of March 2027 is 2027-03-19. Filed estimate and NOT confirmed on purpose: the confirmed opex entries on this calendar carry an 'OCC: theocc.com expiration calendar' source, and theocc.com returned HTTP 403 to a browser-UA curl from this runner today (5,704 bytes, no calendar retrieved), so the primary was not read. A derived date is a derivation, not a source. Promote once the OCC calendar is actually fetched. SHARPENED 2026-09-05 by this event's own initial research, which found a Cboe primary that removes the 'derivation, not a source' objection to the DATE without yet earning a promotion: cboe.com/us/futures/market_statistics/settlement (fetched direct, HTTP 200, 536,802 bytes) carries a live contract row rendered `"VX/G7", " - ", "2027-02-17"` alongside `"VXM/G7"`, and the VIX contract terms define final settlement as the SOQ of the SPX/SPXW series expiring EXACTLY 30 days later — 2027-02-17 + 30 days = 2027-03-19. So Cboe is already listing and daily-settling a product whose terms reference a 2027-03-19 SPX expiration, and the 30-day rule reproduces on every VX/VXM row that page carries from 2026-09 through 2027-04 (09-16 -> 10-16, 10-21 -> 11-20, 11-18 -> 12-18, 12-16 -> 2027-01-15, 01-20 -> 02-19, 02-17 -> 03-19, 03-17 -> 04-16). Status deliberately stays estimate for a narrower reason than before: that evidence dates the INDEX-OPTIONS leg by inference through a contract spec, whereas this entry is TITLED 'triple witching' (index futures + index options + single-stock options), and the other two legs still rest on convention alone. theocc.com re-returned HTTP 403 (5,683 bytes) and cboe.com's own expiration-calendar URLs returned 403/404 to this runner on 2026-09-05. PROMOTION CRITERION, now specific: fetch an OCC or Cboe expiration calendar that lists 2027-03-19 directly
notes: DISCOVERED during the boj-decision-2027-03-18 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05). Tracked here for corridor structure rather than for a new mechanic: March quarterly expiration stacks index rebalancing and roll flows into one session, and this one falls on the day AFTER the Bank of Japan's March 2027 decision (boj-decision-2027-03-18, estimate) and shares its session with Japan's February national CPI (japan-cpi-2027-03-19, estimate, 08:30 JST). Together with the FOMC's first-SEP meeting concluding 2027-03-17 (fomc-2027-03-17, estimate), that is four dated events in three sessions, and the attribution consequence is the reason all four were filed at once: a 2027-03-19 US tape move has an opex explanation, a Japanese-CPI explanation and a two-central-bank explanation before it has a BoJ one. The same trap the boj-decision-2026-12-18 ledger recorded for its own date, one quarter's structure removed. AMENDED 2026-09-05 by this event's own initial research (docs/research/events/opex-2027-03-19.md), which filed three more dated entries into this corridor and found the structure is denser than 'four events in three sessions'. The full sequence is now: S&P Select Sector rebalance reference close Fri 2027-03-12 (sp-rebalance-reference-close-2027-03-12, estimate, SEC-filed rule) -> VIX/VXM March expiration AM-settling Wed 2027-03-17 (vix-expiration-2027-03-17, estimate, Cboe-listed) some five hours BEFORE the 14:00 ET FOMC decision the same day -> BoJ Thu 2027-03-18 -> Japan CPI 08:30 JST + this witching Fri 2027-03-19, whose close carries the single-stock options AND the SEC-dated Select Sector rebalance MOC. The genuinely new find is on the far side: Easter 2027 is early, so Good Friday falls 2027-03-26 (good-friday-market-closure-2027-03-26, estimate, NYSE-sourced), INSIDE the post-witching window and BEFORE quarter-end — the unpin week is 4 sessions, not 5, and the quarter's final week is a 3-session stub.
